reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 uses different ML models on a different alloy (FeNiCrCoCu) without phase-field or GPR. E2 states DFT cannot explicitly evaluate fracture/yield strength, contradicting the premise of a surrogate for these properties. E3 uses transformer models on synthetic data without microstructural inputs. E4 and E5 are irrelevant to the proposed methodology. No evidence supports the use of phase-field descriptors with GPR for this alloy or the claimed accuracy and efficiency gains.
premises: Phase-field simulations can extract mesoscale descriptors (chemical fluctuations, local stiffness) that capture the hierarchical heterostructure of HfNbTiVAl10.
These descriptors can be calibrated within a Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) framework using limited experimental data.
The GPR surrogate model can predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness with high accuracy (errors ~5-10%).
This approach reduces computational cost by a factor of 50-100 compared to full-scale first-principles or MD simulations.
The method is reliable under room temperature, moderate strain rate conditions for the specific hierarchical heterostructure.
